title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Although he was killed, the Dark Soul of Manus was so large and powerful that he was reborn in death, and his soul split into miniscule fragments that retained some will. These pieces began to coalesce once again by absorbing other humanities, becoming the incarnations of different emotions of Manus and then human in shape, with their own self-awareness: Elana was the embodiment of Manus' wrath, Alsanna of his fear, Nadalia of his solitude and Nashandra, the tiniest fragment of Manus, the embodiment of his want. These new entities had some recollection of their father and his dark powers and when the Abyss that they called home was dissipated they scattered across the land. To sustain themselves and seek power, they reached Drangleic where in one way or another they came into contact with the holders of magnificent souls, drawn to their awesome strength.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - notes 
 notes : The Silver Pendant, although not required, can be of great help as it blocks his magic attacks if used with correct timing.

Great Grey Wolf Sif can help in this battle. Whilst Sif's attacks are not very damaging, the extra summon can keep Manus distracted and give the player time to heal. It is wise to only summon Sif after Manus is below half health, to distract him in his harder phase, making it less likely the player will be targeted by the Dark Orb barrage attack.

Sif's summon sign is *inside* the Manus's arena, directly to the left of where the player spawns. As a result, Sif can only be summoned *during* the fight. Thankfully, Sif is summoned instantly after touching the sign, without the usual white phantom-summoning animation. Since it is summoned during the fight it does not increase Manus' Hp.

Similar to the Tin Crystallization Catalyst, it boosts the strength of sorceries, but limits the number of castings.

title: Manus Catalyst
snippet:
Manus Catalyst -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Similarly to the Tin Crystallization Catalyst, the Manus Catalyst greatly boosts the power of spells at the cost of halving their casts (including Pyromancies and Miracles), though this may be offset with use of the Dusk Crown Ring. In addition, the Manus Catalyst also boosts the power of Dark sorceries, based on the player's strength stat.
The strong attack of the Manus Catalyst is quite powerful for a catalyst, but very slow, and uses the Greataxe moveset.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Manus was a primordial human who possessed an extraordinary soul consisting of a viscous, lukewarm lump of gentle humanity, an immense Dark Soul. He was also a sorcerer who used a rough and old wooden catalyst, very crude but large enough to be used as a weapon. His sorceries could grant a fleeting will to the Dark of humanity, induced to relentlessly chase enemies through channeling innate human affinities. Manus also possessed one half of an ancient stone pendant, a precious magical artifact that emanated a distinct, wrenching nostalgia as well as reverence.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - strategies 
 strategies : It is possible for the player to kill Manus outside his fog gate:
#Kill all the surrounding Humanity Phantoms.
#Unequip all armor, then equip a fully upgraded longbow, Feather Arrows, the Symbol of Avarice, the Red Tearstone Ring, and the Hawk Ring.
#Unequip the Symbol of Avarice after the Red Tearstone Ring activates.
#Stand on the right side of the bridge that leads to the fog gate. There are a set of ridges, and on the third from the bridge, Manus's red eyes will be visible.
#Shoot towards the eyes until you successfully hit Manus. Keep shooting until his health is low. Now you have two options:
##Enter the fog door and finish him off.
##Kill him from the ledge. The fog gate will disappear and you'll gain his reward souls. When you approach the platform that Manus usually grabs you off of, you can roll off to land without damage.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: Manus was a sorcerer of Oolacile, and after he died, his body was buried in the caverns beneath the city. 200 to 300 years prior to the journey of the Chosen Undead, the Primordial Serpent Kaathe arrived in Oolacile, in search of a potential Dark Lord following the flooding of New Londo. He manipulated the country to upturn the grave of the primordial man, Manus, buried beneath the dungeons of their city and resurrect him. Manus awakened to find his pendant missing, and was eventually driven into a beastly frenzy as his Dark Soul went wild, transforming him into the "Father of the Abyss".

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: Manus at one point kidnapped Princess Dusk of Oolacile—possibly after her rescue from a Golden Crystal Golem—and imprisoned her deep within the Chasm of the Abyss. In the meantime, his prized pendant came under the possession of Seath the Scaleless and then a Chosen Undead in the future; Manus, driven by his unrelenting search for his pendant, snatched the Undead from the future and brought them into the old Oolacile. There, the Chosen Undead put down the corrupted Knight Artorias and journeyed within the Chasm of the Abyss, where they finally defeated Manus and put him to rest. While Dusk was rescued in the process, she was driven by Elizabeth into thinking that she was saved by Artorias, preserving the legacy of the Wolf Knight. Nevertheless, Dusk came to recognize the Chosen Undead's similarity to the fabled knight, and developed doubts of her own as to her true savior.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Manus may be named for Mannus, the father of mankind in Germanic mythology. According to the Roman writer Tacitus, the Germanic tribes believed a god *Tuisto* sprang from the ground and had a son, *Mannus*, from whom all humans were descended. Manus is also the Latin word for “hand”, alluding to Manus’s massive left hand.
**However a more accurate translation of "深淵の主マヌス" would be "Manus, Lord of the Abyss".

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: As the Abyss spread across the land of Oolacile, Knight Artorias arrived to halt its advance and confront Manus, as the Knight of Gwyn already had experience with fighting the Abyss and its creatures after the events of New Londo and his hunt for the Darkwraiths, and possessed a Silver Pendant that protected him from the Dark. However, Artorias's pendant was stolen by Oolacile's inhabitants and hidden behind an illusory wall, depriving Artorias of protection against Manus's dark sorceries. Together with his trusted companion Sif, Artorias faced Manus but his strength proved insufficient to defeat him, and he succumbed to the Abyss. Injured in the battle, Artorias used his Cleansing Greatshield to form a magic barrier that protected Sif from the Dark. Now corrupted to his soul by the Abyss and with his armor corroded, Artorias was left to fight alone and hold back the treacherous citizens of Oolacile.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: Kaathe, following his failure with the Four Kings, arrived in Oolacile and manipulated its inhabitants into upturning the grave of Manus, a primordial man with an extraordinary Dark Soul and dark sorcery skills, who had been buried beneath the dungeons of their city, and resurrect him. Awakening to find his precious broken pendant missing, Manus was eventually driven mad and his Dark Soul went wild, transforming him into a dark beast eternally seeking his pendant. His immense mass of humanity out of control led to the manifestation of an Abyss that spread, threatening to devour the entire land. The Dark emanating from Manus not only generated countless Humanity Phantoms with a will of their own but also influenced the residents of Oolacile, making their humanity go wild and horribly mutating their bodies, bloating their head and opening them with cracks lined with innumerable tiny red eyeballs and protruding brain parts.

title: Oolacile
snippet:
Oolacile -  Dark Souls - location - lead 
 lead : The lost land of **Oolacile** is a location that no longer exists by the events of *Dark Souls*. Several sources allude to its existence centuries beforehand and its focus on sorceries. Dusk of Oolacile states that the land "was reduced to ashes" long ago.

The later version of the game, *Dark Souls: Prepare to Die Edition*, comes with extra content that takes place in Oolacile 200-300 years before the events of the game, where the Chosen Undead must take the place of Artorias the Abysswalker and rescue Dusk from Manus, Father of the Abyss. During this period, Oolacile is slowly being swallowed by the Abyss. The content was later added as DLC to the console versions of the game as *Artorias of the Abyss*.

title: Gods
snippet:
Gwynevere, Goddess of Sunlight and eldest daughter of Gwyn. She fled Anor Londo prior to the events of *Dark Souls*, after which she married the God Flann, with whom she had several children. By the time of *Dark Souls III*, she married King Oceiros, making her the Queen of Anor Londo's neighbouring kingdom of Lothric, and mothered three of his children, although she has fled this kingdom too by the events of the game.
Gwyndolin, God of the "Dark Moon" and of the "Dark Sun", and lastborn son of Gwyn. Raised in secrecy as a girl, he is a hybrid likely mothered by Crossbreed Priscilla, and the last God left in Anor Londo and Lordran by the events of *Dark Souls*, although he remains perceived as somewhat of a minor deity, acting from the shadows, including by creating an illusion of Gwynevere. By the events of *Dark Souls III*, he succeeded Lloyd as ruler of the Gods, and reigned from Irithyll, their new seat of power he built atop old Anor Londo.

title: Lore
snippet:
Soon after, the deities began leaving Lordran. Gwyndolin was the only one of Gwyn's children to stay behind...

Seath, who became obsessed with his research and experiments, amassed countless tomes and was eventually driven mad - at least, how normal people see it - by his research, becoming the founder of sorcery.

At least a thousand years pass and the events of "Dark Souls" begin to unfold...

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Nashandra began her life as a small fragment of Manus, Father of the Abyss. When Manus was defeated, he was reborn as many fragments varying in sizes. Nashandra was the incarnation of her "father's" want, and thus began desiring what she did not have: power.

Nashandra travelled to the land of Drangleic, and set her sights on its powerful ruler, King Vendrick. Deciding to seduce Vendrick, Nashandra assumed a human form of unparalleled beauty and warned him of a supposed looming threat beyond the sea: the Giants. She convinced him to invade the land of the giants to claim their power, which Vendrick did successfully. Vendrick then made Nashandra his queen, and under their leadership, Drangleic entered into a Dark-like peace. The rulership of Drangleic however, was not enough to quell Nashandra’s want, and she desired an even greater power: the First Flame, which she intended to claim for herself by using Vendrick and the Throne of Want.

title: Nashandra
snippet: When Drangleic was ravaged by the second war with the giants and the spread of the Undead Curse, Vendrick came to realize the true nature and identity of Nashandra, and what she had coveted all along. Knowing that his time was short and that his queen had to be stopped, Vendrick created several impasses that would prevent Nashandra from seizing the throne, and sealed himself away in the Undead Crypt. This left Nashandra the sole ruler of Drangleic, albeit without much left to rule at all, as the kingdom had been all but destroyed.

title: Nashandra
snippet: Left without a king and with no means to claim the Throne of Want, Nashandra’s plans were stalled until the arrival of the Bearer of the Curse, an undead powerful enough to defeat the Four Old Ones and gain access to Drangleic Castle. Nashandra manipulated the Bearer of the Curse into opening the way to the Throne of Want by aiding them in seizing the Throne of Want. She directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Undead Crypt, suggesting that they put an end to the now-hollowed King Vendrick and claim his ring. She then directs the Bearer of the Curse to journey to Aldia's Keep to acquire the Ashen Mist Heart, and warns them that the Ancient Dragon there is no more than a prop and a false deity. At last, she directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Forest of Fallen Giants to visit the memories of the Giants and obtain the last key to the Throne: the Giant's Kinship.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Once the Bearer of the Curse has finally cleared the way to the Throne and acquired the means to access it, Nashandra will intercept them and reveal her true form. She then declares the Bearer of the Curse worthy to assume her intended role for Vendrick, to have their power usurped by her so she can claim the throne for herself.

The Bearer of the Curse has grown too strong however, and Nashandra falls at their hand.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - lead 
 lead : **Nashandra** or **Queen Nashandra** is a boss and the main antagonist of *Dark Souls II*. She is fought at the end of the Throne of Want area, only after the player has obtained the Giant's Kinship; if the Throne Watcher and Defender have not already been defeated, Nashandra's boss fight will trigger automatically after theirs.

Although she is the final boss of the base game, the *Scholar of the First Sin* expansion added Aldia as a potential "true" final boss, whose battle triggers after Nashandra's if conditions are met. Prior to her boss fight, she appears as a special character in human form atop Drangleic Castle, where she can be talked to from afar.

title: Elana, the Squalid Queen
snippet:
Elana, the Squalid Queen -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Elana, the Squalid Queen, like Nashandra, was a fragment of Manus, Father of the Abyss, supposedly a fragment representing the trait of wrath. Regaining her form, she became Elana, and later wife of the Sunken King. It is unknown if she designed to betray the Sunken King or if she truly loved him, but one day Sir Yorgh and his Drakeblood Knights besieged Shulva, defeating the Sunken King and awakening Sinh, the Slumbering Dragon, who then let forth a toxic cloud which annihilated the whole city.

Somehow, Elana survived the siege, and became furious and vengeful for her city's destruction and possibly her husband's death. She took on her true form and now accompanies Sinh, accruing souls for the day of her vengeance.

title: Alsanna, Silent Oracle
snippet:
Alsanna, Silent Oracle -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Alsanna is a mysterious child of the Dark, one of the many fragments of Manus, Father of the Abyss. At an unknown point, she traveled to the northern kingdom of Eleum Loyce, ruled by the Ivory King, and devoted herself to him as his oracle. An ancient Chaos was discovered deep below the land, so in an attempt to appease the raging flame the Ivory King built a great cathedral at its mouth and Alsanna prayed in silent vigilance. The attempt was unsuccessful, and the flames still raged.

title: Alsanna, Silent Oracle
snippet:
Eventually, the Ivory King sensed the degradation of his soul and left Eleum Loyce without a word, leaving everything to Alsanna. Upon his departure, he gifted her an intertwined blade of shadow and light, revealing to her that he had already known about her Dark nature. He traveled deep into the Chaos for one final assault but was eventually devoured by its flames. In a last ditch attempt to quell the fiery Chaos, the Gates of Eleum Loyce were opened, allowing the cold harsh blizzard to consume the kingdom whole.

In spite of all this, Alsanna bravely chose to remain and devoted herself to prayer to appease the raging flame in memory of her loving lord. All the while hoping that despite all odds, he might perhaps one day return.

title: Alsanna, Silent Oracle
snippet:
Alsanna, Silent Oracle -  Dark Souls II - character - loyce_knight_souls 
 loyce_knight_souls : After the King's defeat, Alsanna will mention: *"The knights of Eleum Loyce were swallowed by the Chaos... where their souls still remain. I pray for their deliverance."* This prompts the side quest to collect Loyce Souls in exchange for pieces of the Loyce Set and eventually her soul.

Every time a Loyce Knight soul is returned to her, she says: *"I sense a knight's joyous elation. Kind visitor, please accept my gratitude."* Progressively, the formations of ice blocking the stairs will break the more souls are returned. Once 15 souls have been returned, she states:

Once 50 souls have been collected, the final pieces of ice break, allowing the player to meet her. She sits at the top of the staircase, kneeling in prayer. When spoken to, her dialogue will allude to her sisters, Nashandra, Elana and Nadalia:

title: Nadalia, Bride of Ash
snippet:
Nadalia, Bride of Ash -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Nadalia, like Elana and Nashandra, is a fragment of Manus after the latter was defeated by the Chosen Undead centuries beforehand. She came to Brume Tower in search of the Old Iron King, either out of genuine affection or to simply force his kingdom to crumble. But when she arrived, she found that the king had been slain, and his kingdom left in shambles.

Falling into despair, Nadalia split her soul apart and stored those fragments within various ashen idols throughout the hollowed and empty Brume Tower. Upon doing this, she erected a black fog that consumed the tower and brought back the deceased soldiers and warriors, bewitching them into defending her. Many knights of outside lands came to the tower to steal the stores of iron within Brume Tower, but Nadalia's idols both bewitched the ones who were willing to serve her, and destroyed the ones who would attempt to defy her.

title: Nadalia, Bride of Ash
snippet:
Sometime after his defeat at the hands of Velstadt, Sir Raime of Drangleic came to Brume Tower in search of greater power, and eventually came to view Nadalia as a mother figure. Rather than purge the black fog, Raime instead chose to live alongside the fog, and became Nadalia's loyal guardian.

Her original body can be found at the bottom of the tower past Raime, clutching the Crown of the Old Iron King and sitting upon his throne.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
The Bearer of the Curse will journey through the Black Gulch to find the fallen kingdom of Shulva, Sanctum City, once ruled by the Sunken King. The king ruled the city, centred around the worship of a slumbering dragon known as Sinh, until his kingdom was invaded by the Drakeblood Knights lead by Sir Yorgh, who sought to claim the dragon's blood. Sir Yorgh slew the king, and awoke the dragon, which proceeded to kill him and lay waste to the city with its poison. The Bearer of the Curse slays Elana, the Squalid Queen, a child of the Abyss, and the dragon Sinh to claim the Sunken King's crown.

Next, the Bearer of the Curse returns to the Old Iron Kingdom, to seek the Old Iron King's crown. Finding the kingdom under the sway of another child of the Abyss, Nadalia, Bride of Ash, the Bearer braves their way through the ruined towers to find the Fume Knight, who guards the crown of the Old Iron King.

title: Soul of Nashandra
snippet:
Soul of Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - item - description 
 description : Soul of Nashandra, Queen of Drangleic.

Nashandra was born of the Dark with an insatiable lust for strength.

Use the special soul of this prisoner of desire to acquire numerous souls, or to create something of great worth.

title: Soul of Alsanna, Silent Oracle
snippet:
Soul of Alsanna, Silent Oracle -  Dark Souls II - item - description 
 description : Soul of Alsanna, oracle of Eleum Loyce, who prays in silent vigilance.

This child of Dark, in reverence of the apocalypse, devotes herself to a ritual in hopes of appeasing the raging flame.

The wondrous soul of this augur of fear can be used to acquire numerous souls, or to create something of great worth.

title: Throne of Want
snippet:
At a certain moment during his reign, Nashandra came to Drangleic, she coveted the Throne of Want and the power of the First Flame, and seduced Vendrick in order to use him as a means to accomplish her goal, becoming his queen.

Much time later, after Drangleic was ravaged due to both the war with the Giants and the undead curse, which all of Vendrick’s and Aldia’s plans to cure were in vain, Vendrick found out about Nashandra's plan: to use the throne to claim the First Flame for herself. Vendrick reacted quickly and sent the Throne Watcher and the Throne Defender to guard the throne. He then fled to the Undead Crypt, where he eventually went Hollow, to keep his ring and soul from the wrong hands. He did all this in an attempt to stop Nashandra.

title: Fume Knight
snippet: Having decided to leave Drangleic behind, Raime roamed the lands as a knight without purpose until his travels led him to the haunted Brume Tower where he found a child of dark Nadalia. In her however, he found a new purpose as well as the figure his previous lord was unable to provide. Instead of expunging the black fog, he embraced it and became her loyal guardian and champion. In return for his service as well as company in solitude, Raime was entrusted with a fragment of her soul which haunted his blade. As the Fume Knight, Raime would remain at his post to guard his new master from intruders, for so long that even he was buried under the ash.

title: The Old Chaos
snippet:
The Old Chaos -  Dark Souls II - location - lore 
 lore : In ancient times, the Witch of Izalith attempted to recreate the First Flame with the Lord Soul that was in her possession. Instead, she spawned a corrupted fire known as the Flame of Chaos. When she failed to control the new flame, it consumed her and molded her into a twisted being known as the Bed of Chaos, the source of all demons.

Eventually, the Bed of Chaos was destroyed by the Chosen Undead, but the flames of Chaos lived on. At an unknown point, the flames of Chaos were discovered deep below the kingdom of Eleum Loyce. In an attempt to appease the raging flame, the Ivory King built a great cathedral at its mouth and the oracle of Eleum Loyce, Alsanna, prayed in silent vigilance. The attempt was unsuccessful and the flames still raged.
